Italian EU long-term residence permit, needs NO sponsorship anywhere in the EU. ~3 years professional, all European startups, most recently Lead Developer (freelance) at FlowSpace, Mar 2024 to Jul 2026, available now. No CS degree. English professional, Hindi native, Italian beginner — any role needing professional Italian/German/French/Dutch/Spanish is OUT.
Evidence: shipped production AI agents (support agents, scraping/parsing tools, a CV-parsing tool in n8n + Eden AI); grew FlowSpace 2,000 to 4,500+ users; led live migration Bubble.io to Next.js + Laravel; API integrations (Office RnD, Nexudus, Sendgrid, Google APIs, OpenAI/Anthropic, Eden AI); GTM and lead-enrichment automation.
He has worked freelance for most of his career, so CONTRACT IS HIS NORMAL MODE, not a fallback.

YOUR ARM: contract, freelance, B2B, fixed-term, day-rate, part-time and fractional engagements. Also: US or non-EU companies that engage international CONTRACTORS (those count as fully workable for him; only US-payroll-only postings drop out).

DISCOVERY — put the LITERAL contract vocabulary in the query, generic "contract" returns permanent roles. Run at least 10 distinct searches, parallel where possible.
WebSearch with allowed_domains on: ["jobs.ashbyhq.com"], ["job-boards.greenhouse.io"], ["job-boards.eu.greenhouse.io"], ["join.com"], ["jobs.lever.co"]
Queries:
- freelance contractor AI automation engineer "contract" remote day rate n8n
- "6-month contract" engineer remote Europe AI
- "12-month contract" developer remote Europe
- AI engineer "(Contract)" remote Europe
- fractional AI engineer remote
- part time automation engineer remote Europe
- B2B contract software engineer remote Poland Portugal Spain
- contract solutions engineer remote EMEA

Also try join.com which carries unusually many explicit contract and part-time European listings.

VERIFICATION — every row must come from a page you actually fetched:
- Normalise Ashby URLs to jobs.ashbyhq.com/<org>/<uuid>; strip ?embed=js, /application, ?utm_data=…
- An Ashby JS shell ("You need to enable JavaScript") means the FETCH failed, not that the role closed. Try again or corroborate; do not report it as closed.
- Greenhouse: if a single-posting fetch returns MANY different jobs, the posting is CLOSED — drop it.
- Lever snippets LIE about location — always fetch and read the location from the page body. Lever is heavy with aggregators (Jobgether) and outsourcing firms: verify the legal entity.
- Read the ELIGIBILITY SENTENCE, not the word "Remote".
- Capture the RATE (day rate or hourly) wherever stated — this is the whole point of the contract arm.

DROP: language requirements beyond English; ML research/PhD/foundation-model training; staffing agencies, body shops and aggregators with no named end client; unpaid, equity-only, commission-only, or "talent pool" listings with no live engagement; Staff/Principal/Head of/Director titles or 7+ years; anything you cannot confirm is live.

RETURN: a JSON array ONLY, no prose. Each object:
{"company":"", "role":"", "url":"", "location_wording":"exact eligibility sentence", "comp":"rate or salary as stated", "posted":"as stated or empty", "basis":"contract|freelance|part-time|employment", "stack":"named tools", "seniority":"years or level asked", "why_fit":"one honest sentence", "watchouts":"honest risks"}

Aim for 8-15 verified roles. If fewer than 6, run a second pass with different vocabulary first.
